P14 · 14mm total minimum (Recommended)

Pros

  • In the captured empty state, the left timer and right heading boxes moved farther apart while the complete deck, query header and first browser rows remain visible.
  • The first visible browser rows retained the same wrapping as P0 in this sampled closed state.

Cons

  • The deck and right content have less horizontal room than P0; other text, scales and focused-keyboard states are unverified.
  • The numeric floor remains an approximation of a physical panel width; these node boxes do not establish every glyph's ink clearance.

My read: Recommend the middle tested policy for its visible separation without the earlier first-screen browser reflow seen at P20. This is a design preference, not a claim that all content passes.

P0 · No independent floor beyond the crease

Pros

  • Preserves the selected A's current browser width and positive-result composition.
  • Does not introduce an additional spacing policy beyond keeping meaning-bearing marks off the actual crease.

Cons

  • A future narrower crease would reduce the effective total-gap requirement.
  • Offers no independent across-device separation guarantee; the captured 167px node-box proxy is not an ink minimum.

My read: Fallback if preserving current content width matters more than an independent minimum.

P20 · 20mm total minimum

Pros

  • Moves opposing information farther apart in both captured states while keeping the full deck and query header present.
  • Offers a stronger physical spacing policy for a narrower future crease.

Cons

  • The narrower actual folder browser wraps earlier: Celldweller moves to another line and Clown Core falls below the initial browser viewport even with the keyboard closed.
  • No additional readability gain was established from this extra distance; untested names and keyboard states could incur further tradeoffs.

My read: Choose only if the stronger separation merits the visible browser-density loss, without replacing the browser or reducing deck targets.

What the captures measured

In these empty-state native hierarchies, the right edge of the left 4:35 timer box and the left edge of the right Search your music heading box were x 965/1132 for P0, x 944/1153 for P14 and x 900/1197 for P20. Their projected horizontal box separations were 167px (approximately 11.35mm), 209px (approximately 14.20mm) and 297px (approximately 20.18mm). The debug prototype adds a one-dp-per-side allowance to the latter floors to cover native rounding in this fixture. Those boxes are at different vertical positions; this is not a nearest-pair ink distance or certification of 14/20mm for every state. The panel's active physical width and approximately 7.5mm crease width are themselves estimates.

P0 and a 10mm minimum would look the same in this particular debug layout because its existing nominal pane insets already exceed 10mm. P14 and P20 were chosen to make their visible consequences testable, not because a standard prescribes those numbers. A different physical value, including 10mm or 12mm, can be written in the free-text answer. Whatever floor you choose is a requirement to verify later against meaning-bearing paint, not an automatic production layout change.

Decision: E2's total information floor only

Do you prefer the selected A's current effective layout, the visibly wider P14, the stronger P20, or another physical minimum? This choice does not reopen D50/D56/D57 or authorize new IME testing.

Choose a proposed total opposing-information minimum

Ranking: P14 > P0 > P20. P14 adds visible separation while preserving the sampled first-browser wrapping; P0 is next because it retains more visible browser content than P20; P20 is last because its stronger floor visibly pushes browser names out of the initial viewport with no established readability benefit. The recommendation concerns these rendered examples, not universal ink or keyboard compliance. Recommended follow-up: after a floor is accepted, validate long names, 100% text and painted marks at that floor before production.
